peer.limitation: Leaf PCs and in-range consumer frames independently symbolized from recorded MMAP addresses and matching ELF. Return addresses adjusted by minus1. Stop at first unmapped/bogus frame. Foundation/system binaries were not rebuilt with frame pointers; mapped frames may also be incomplete or misleading. Partial chains are diagnostic clues, not exact inclusive percentages or a decomposition of the formal latency gap.

method: Separate software sampling,4000 complete holdout episodes per route, matching current send/recv fixture. Fresh HTTP2/consumer TUs with frame pointers, cached foundation unchanged. 1997Hz cpu-clock:u, no hardware PMU or formal timing; all payload/protocol/cleanup oracles passed. Profiling all process threads includes startup and inactive harness overhead.
conclusion: Frame-pointer recording recovered some usable source callchains without installing/rebuilding profiler tooling. They implicate ordinary flush/receive/body-consume paths as next diagnostic locations; they do not establish the root cause or a scheduler percentage. Product HTTP2 unchanged, stage3 formal residual still unresolved. Do not rank total sample counts or sum inclusive nodes.
tool_limit: Header inspection reports Invalid HEADER_EVENT_DESC and event description unavailable. Event samples/MMAP records decode; selected leaf/caller PCs were resolved independently with matching image and addr2line. Unknown/invalid suffixes are retained and excluded after their first invalid frame; mapped pointers can still be misleading when cached frames omit FP. No complete-stack claim.
